question: Is a versioned regulatory corpus with reliable validity intervals (in-force start/end dates) and time-stamped queries actually available or constructible at reasonable cost?
description: The framework and its benchmark require per-passage validity metadata and queries with target dates. Existing temporal benchmarks cover ESG disclosures and SEC filings; availability of equivalent amendment/validity metadata for statutes or regulations is unverified.
rationale: Retrieved temporal benchmarks are in ESG and financial domains; no retrieved work confirms an equivalent amended-statute benchmark with validity intervals.
resolution: Partially resolved in the direction of feasibility: the legal-retrieval literature names the European Legislation Identifier as representing date of entry into force and date of applicability, so in-force validity intervals are derivable for at least some jurisdictions, and the problem of distinguishing valid time from transaction time is recognized as a required corpus property. What remains unverified is passage-level (clause) validity granularity and the availability of time-stamped queries with ground-truth in-force versions, so benchmark construction is still a real but no longer speculative cost.
